transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Nguyen (VanguardX CTO), Aisha Bello (VanguardX ML Eng), Jon Park (VanguardX Infra)

Summary:
Quick readout of week-2 pilot bench results vs their incumbent, triage of the 95th percentile latency spike during peak, and agreement on routing/playbook + next steps to validate VPC path. Shared artifacts: benchmark_sheet_vanguardx.xlsx (link in notes), routing_playbook_v1.pdf, SOC2_and_KMS_overview.pdf.

Topics:
- p50/p95 comparison vs baseline provider
- throughput stability under 2000 RPS burst
- KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior
- quantization impact on quality vs latency tradeoff
- VPC peering and encryption (KMS) for private pilot

---- Transcript body ----
[00:00] Lena: alright good to go? Hey everyone, uh thanks for making time. This is Lena from Redwood, I'm with Samir, our systems engineer. Today we want to walk through the week two bench readout and then dig into the p95 spike Marcus flagged.
[00:28] Marcus: yeah thanks Lena, big agenda for us. we've been comparing the numbers you sent, and overall nice improvements but that 95th kept us up last night so want to understand root cause and next steps.
[00:45] Samir: cool, I'll share my screen — um — the sheet I posted is benchmark_sheet_vanguardx.xlsx, link in the calendar notes. quick TL;DR: across the standard conversational prompt set (avg seq ~180 tokens), Redwood p50 is ~60ms faster than IncumbentCloudAI, p95 is ~90ms lower in most steady-state windows.
[01:12] Aisha: when you say p95 lower, are we looking at the same batching config? our baseline uses 32-token batches at 80ms max latency target.
[01:22] Samir: good call — in these tests we matched batching to your baseline: we used target batch of 4–8 requests (dynamic), request timeout 1200ms, and two paths — hosted default and dedicated-slot with preferred GPU kernels. the dedicated run is where we saw the best p95.
[01:40] Jon: can you remind us the hardware profile of your dedicated slot? the baseline is running mixed A100 and T4 pools.
[01:49] Samir: dedicated slot for this pilot was a single H100 slice (v2 equivalent in infra) with our kernel selection tuned to the model. we also enabled int8 quantization profile for speed on the dedicated run — for quality-sensitive prompts we also did an fp16 run.
[02:10] Marcus: aha int8 — okay. did you see any quality regressions on our evaluation prompts? we sent a couple of edge-case prompts yesterday.
[02:18] Samir: we ran the Aisha-samples, quality delta was <0.7% on Rouge-style metric for the chosen quant profile. there were two prompts where repetitiveness increased slightly — those are in the sheet under 'quality-anomalies'.
[02:35] Aisha: yep saw that. one of them is related to list enumerations. we'll mark those as failing for the pilot acceptance criteria.
[02:42] Lena: thanks — we'll flag them. next, the p95 spike — can you walk us through when that happened and under what traffic shape?
[02:50] Marcus: spike occurs around 08:45 local during our internal peak; traffic pattern is a sudden fanout — ~2k RPS sustained for ~30s then drop. p95 jumps to ~650ms in our baseline runs, your hosted runs had p95 ~540ms but we saw a jump to ~900ms for one window in the dedicated test last night.
[03:13] Samir: right — we pulled trace logs. two things stood out: a KV cache miss storm during traffic ramp (we call it 'cold prefix' effect) and a short-lived routing rebalancing event where requests were routed to a fallback variant while an older model checkpoint finished a compaction job. 
[03:34] Jon: compaction job? sounds like infra-level maintenance — can you explain?
[03:38] Samir: sorry yes — it's related to our internal model cache/optimizer that compacts older KV shards to reduce memory; it should be background and non-blocking but in this run the compaction delayed the kernel swap and triggered a brief queueing window. that's on us to harden.
[03:53] Lena: to be clear, that's not the customer KV cash — that's Redwood's internal KV node behavior, right?
[03:58] Samir: correct, internal. but observable in the traces as queue time at the long-tail.
[04:05] Marcus: okay that explains the one-off. For acceptance, we need deterministic p95 under our peak. What mitigations do you recommend?
[04:12] Samir: immediate: pin the routing policy to dedicated-slot only for the 48hr load window (no automatic fallback), increase pre-warm for KV prefixes tied to your prompt set, and disable compaction during the test window. medium-term: change compaction scheduling and add backpressure isolation so compaction doesn't steal CPU cycles from inference workers.
[04:34] Aisha: how do we pin routing? is that a config change we can set?
[04:38] Samir: yes it's a route policy. I can create a canary policy that forces sticky routing to the dedicated pool and disable fallbacks. I'll add it to the routing_playbook_v1.pdf and push the change before the rerun.
[04:52] Jon: about VPC peering — if we run these tests over our VPC path, is there any added latency? we need an estimate.
[04:59] Samir: there will be some network RTT but in our experience with VPC peering it's small — typically 8–15ms added roundtrip depending on region. we'll measure it during the side-by-side run. also note TLS and KMS calls for envelope encryption add a tiny handshake cost per session; we can reuse session tokens to amortize.
[05:20] Marcus: we require KMS integration and customer-managed keys for the private slot — do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[05:26] Lena: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. we have the integration doc SOC2_and_KMS_overview.pdf in the notes; we'll send examples of SAML metadata and how audit logs appear.
[05:39] Marcus: great. another question — unit cost. how does cost compare at peak? baseline quotes were roughly 20% lower per-token but with higher latency. can you provide cost per million tokens across profiles?
[05:50] Lena: we're preparing a detailed cost model in the sheet. quick numbers: for the int8 dedicated profile used in the test, Redwood estimated $X per 1M tokens (we'll put exact number in the sheet), when you include prefix caching and batching savings the effective unit cost is closer to their number for conversational workloads. we'll call out where caching reduces billable tokens.
[06:10] Aisha: on caching — how do you handle shared prefixes and privacy? our prompts sometimes include PII in prefixes.
[06:18] Samir: good point — we support per-customer KV namespaces and optional encryption at rest. by default hosted caches are ephemeral and not used for persistent PII storage; for Private you control the KV lifecycle. we'll include the privacy config snippet in the notes.
[06:34] Marcus: can we see the raw traces for the spike window? timeline and stack traces?
[06:38] Samir: yes attached in the spreadsheet as 'trace_2026-12-04-08_45_window.log' — it's summarized in the first sheet. I'll also share a flamegraph link in the doc.
[06:49] Jonas: [crosstalk] jon: yeah saw that — the trace indicates queue latency at the runtime layer not at network.
[06:55] (small laughter)
[07:00] Samir: so next steps for triage: I propose we do a 48hr dedicated-only run with compaction off, pre-warm the KV prefixes 15 minutes before the window, and run your ramp profile with an explicit 2k RPS 30s spike. we will collect p50/p90/p95/99 and token counts.
[07:17] Marcus: sounds reasonable. timeline?
[07:20] Samir: we can provision two dedicated slots by tomorrow if quota approved; Lena will follow up with provisioning ticket.
[07:27] Lena: yep I'll kick that off now. Samir, do you need anything from Jon to submit the quota?
[07:32] Samir: just confirmation of IP ranges and VPC peering contact — Jon said he'd provide.
[07:36] Jon: I'll drop that in the ticket by EOD.
[07:40] Aisha: one more technical — the baseline provider had aggressive kernel batching that occasionally increased jitter; are you using continuous batching or per-request batching?
[07:50] Samir: Redwood runtime uses continuous batching with dynamic cutoff based on latency SLOs; we tune the cutoff per-model and can force deterministic small-batch mode for low-jitter workloads. for this run we'll push deterministic batching so you see stable tail-latency.
[08:06] Marcus: and quantization? is int8 always used on dedicated?
[08:10] Samir: not always. quant profile is selected per-route. int8 gives good p95 reduction but we keep an fp16 fallback for quality-critical routes. we'll annotate which prompts used which profile in the sheet.
[08:20] Lena: quick check — acceptance criteria recap: p95 under 600ms during your 2k RPS spike window, no quality regressions on the 5 failing prompts after tuning, and KMS/HSM set up for the private slot. everyone okay with that?
[08:33] Marcus: agreed.
[08:35] Aisha: yes.
[08:36] Jon: yep.
[08:38] Samir: noted. I'll also add a defensive routing rule so if p95 exceeds threshold we don't failover to a cheaper model variant automatically — we want predictable behavior for this test.
[08:49] Marcus: perfect. on the competitor note, they had a fallback that hid errors but increased token cost — we don't want that.
[08:56] Lena: understood.
[09:00] (longer section of technical debug and screen sharing; transcript sampling)
[10:12] Samir: showing the flamegraph now — you can see the small hot path where compaction kicked in (red block), queue time spiked for 4 seconds.
[10:35] Aisha: okay makes sense. can you annotate the sheet with the exact commits/versions of the runtime used for the dedicated slot? we need to match the baseline engineer's requests.
[10:45] Samir: yes, sheet has runtime_rev: r2026.11.8-seq-opt. I'll add a short changelog note.
[11:00] Marcus: final question — SLA and rollback plan if we commit to dedicated slot for production? do you support automatic fallback to hosted with graceful degradation?
[11:09] Lena: yes, we support configurable rollouts: canary, A/B, and hard fallback. for production we recommend a canary with automatic fallback to a vetted fallback model variant that preserves degradation characteristics. for this pilot we're purposely disabling auto fallback to keep the experiment controlled.
[11:30] Jon: ok good.
[11:34] Lena: great — recap of next steps: Lena will send annotated sheet + logs by 12/07, Samir will request dedicated slots and set routing policy, Jon will supply VPC/IP info by 12/08, Aisha will send final prompt set and failing cases by 12/06. we'll schedule the 48hr dedicated-only run once provisioning is confirmed.
[11:58] Marcus: thanks all. one last thing — can your cost model show incremental savings from prefix caching vs naive token billing? that's important for our finance team.
[12:10] Lena: yes we'll add a 'cache-savings' tab in the sheet with examples.
[12:20] Marcus: ok done. thanks everyone, talk soon.
